profile.reading: a fired transition is followed by trigger-less (completion) transitions until none is enabled, bounded at 64 chase steps per driving step. The bound is a BUDGET, not a fixpoint: a chase that spends it stops mid-run and says so. A trigger-less transition out of a composite state is enabled only once its active substate is a final state (SysML v2 Part 1 §9.2.11.2.1: completion follows the substates); a simple state completes after its entry/do.

innermost active substate first — the enabled transition leaving the deepest state on the active stack wins; within one state, declaration order. The explorer keeps the rule and branches only on the tie-break it does not decide: every transition enabled at that innermost level, never one an inner state beats.

to the least common ancestor of the source and the target, and every transition is external: the source and every active state below it are exited, then each state above the source that does not also hold the target, innermost first; the effect runs; then the states that hold the target and did not stay active are entered, outermost first, down to the target and its initial substate. So a step out of a composite leaves it, and a self-transition, a step to an ancestor, or a step from a composite into one of its own substates exits that state and enters it again. A step whose target sits in no chain of the machine's states — its own root, or a node under an action — has no such ancestor and is taken by neither side: the explorer refuses the machine and the interpreter stops before the step. So is a step across the machine's boundary — into a nested `state def`, into another machine, or out of one.
shallow, and by parent map: leaving a composite state records its last-active child, and re-entry resumes that child only where the composite is marked as a history state.

a parallel STATE nested in an ordinary machine, and a parallel MACHINE ROOT (the machine itself marked parallel, whose child states are its regions), are performed concurrently (SysML v2 §7.18.2), by the interpreter and by the explorer alike: every region is entered at its own start, an event is offered to every region in declaration order, each region takes its own first-declared enabled transition (all of them are explored where several are enabled), a region with none stays, each region sees the store the previous one left, and leaving the parallel state exits every region. The completions come AFTER the event, in the interpreter and in the explorer alike: an event is offered to every region, at every depth, each taking its event transition, and only then are the trigger-less (completion) transitions chased, regions in declaration order, nested regions before the region that holds them, so a region's completion never shows in the view another region has of the same event (SysML v2 performs the regions concurrently within one step). A region that is itself a parallel state has no states of its own: its substates are regions of it, entered at once. A region whose active states end in a parallel state of its own enters that state's regions too, so the active regions form a tree, and the declaration order is FLATTENED depth first: a region, then the regions of the parallel state it ends in, then its next sibling (a region's own transitions and its nested regions never both take one event, which is refused); leaving a nested parallel state exits its regions before it. The interpreter applies the regions in ONE fixed declaration order, where the specification fixes none, so the explorer, where the regions are COUPLED (one writes an attribute another reads or writes), explores EVERY order of them (each region still takes its own innermost enabled transitions, each alternative explored; identical results merged; at most 4 regions, more are refused): its result there is a superset of the interpreter's runs, and a witness is replayed through the interpreter (the transitions each event fires, in declaration order, and the leaves it ends in) and published only if it replays: a witness whose path applies coupled regions in another order is withheld, with that reason. Uncoupled regions give the same result in every order, so one order is explored. A refusal in one region (a step the interpreter does not take) stops the whole run, as the regions are performed together, and a run is complete when every region stands at a final state. A parallel state is complete when every one of its regions stands at a final state of its own, and a trigger-less transition out of it (a parallel machine root: out of the machine, to one of its states) is then taken, after every region is exited, with its guard read at that moment; before then it is not taken. Also refused, with a reason: a history state inside, a transition between regions, a step into a region, an entry action naming a start, an event taken both by a region and by a transition leaving the parallel state, and a timed transition in a region — all verification/behaviour-unsupported-construct, never exhaustive.

profile.reading: none. There is no event pool: `triggerEquals` is an exact string match, and an event no enabled transition accepts is dropped at the step that offered it.

discrete. `after(n)` is a dwell measured against an integer clock that only an explicit time step advances. The explorer advances no clock: it offers each `after(n)` label as a named event, which over-approximates time — a state reachable only after a dwell is treated as reachable, so the unreachable and dead lists stay lower bounds.
